Kelkab Ltd. Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Cloudio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer suited to tracking leaders; lightly raced in similar company and has course form on Good ground, though 111 days off is a query and only one win from five similar-going runs.

runners_data.name: Gino Bella
runners_data.note: Listed as prominent but this is the confirmed front-runner who will lead from flag; the STYLE_FIT tag flags he is out of role here and should be respected only as the pace-maker, not a likely winner.

runners_data.name: Eaglewood
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse returning after 277 days off; handles Good ground well with eight runs on similar going including a win, and the step back to 2m1f suits — the layoff is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Jay Pee M
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has struggled to complete recently (B on latest run); six runs on Good ground yield just one placing, and the 22f trip was beyond him last time so 2m1f looks more appropriate.

runners_data.name: Laurie Blue
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a significant booking for a hold-up operator whose ten Good-ground runs show one win and one place; the hg:tp headgear is noted and a fresh run here after 40 days could sharpen him up.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged for fading in finishes; 317 days off the track is a serious concern, and her record on Good ground of one win from fifteen attempts doesn't inspire confidence even if she returns fit.

runners_data.name: Northern Ruler
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner flagged as a fader; ran only eight days ago and that quick turnaround combined with a poor 0W1P record on Good ground over sixteen furlongs makes improvement hard to project.

runners_data.name: Dictionary Corner
runners_data.note: Unclassified style, so treated as a wildcard; form of RP8-66 includes a refused/pulled-up entry and six finishes on Good ground without a placing — hard to trust at this level.

runners_data.name: Kelly's Cosmos
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a trainer booking on a one-from-twelve recent strike rate; form shows a third place from sixteen furlongs on Heavy, and Good ground hasn't produced a win from nine attempts.

runners_data.name: Urban War
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has finished in the first five only once in Good-ground outings; the hg:t headgear is retained and four zeros since October 2024 put this horse firmly in the non-recommended bracket.

runners_data.name: Footstepstoglory
runners_data.note: In reality a genuine hold-up specialist, but with so many closers unable to get to the rear, he is likely to find himself in a more forward position than ideal — a first run at this trip in 265 days adds fitness doubt.

runners_data.name: Let It Settle
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up type whose last five finishes read 11-14-12-13-14; the fader flag and the series of zeros give little basis to expect a reversal, and being bumped into a midfield role won't help his cause.

runners_data.name: Maxicourt
runners_data.note: Showed some ability when second on Good ground earlier in career, but a pulled-up run last time and the reality that he is a hold-up horse unlikely to find his preferred position in this traffic suggest he is vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Theanniversary Man
runners_data.note: Has won twice in recent form (1-1) and possesses the strongest recent form of the redistributed hold-up group; the question is whether he can thread through from a midfield slot that isn't his natural home — 31 days fresh is fine.

runners_data.name: Bob The Builder
runners_data.note: A 315-day absence for a hold-up runner who fades and is rated 86 makes this very hard to assess; distance experience is over longer trips (20-24f) and the switch back to 2m1f is unproven.

runners_data.name: Getaway Henry
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won last time out at 16f on Good ground and has two wins and four places on similar going; hg:b (blinkers) retained, in-form and well-placed to press Gino Bella from the front.

runners_data.name: Bruise Hill
runners_data.note: Holds up and fades — a combination that is problematic in a 26-runner field; three Good-ground runs all show mid-teen finishes and a bumped-to-midfield position won't resolve those structural issues.

runners_data.name: Drumadeise
runners_data.note: Three runs, all zeros, all at 16f on Good ground — no evidence of ability at this level, and being a true hold-up horse forced into midfield only adds positional compromise.

runners_data.name: El Regalo
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner flagged as a fader who has never placed on Good ground from nine attempts; the hg:b headgear is a first-time application here but offers thin encouragement given the form.

runners_data.name: Lunar Landscape
runners_data.note: Six finishes on Good ground include three placings and a recent 6th; a genuine hold-up horse who will be shuffled into midfield in this traffic, making it very hard to exploit whatever finishing kick he has.

runners_data.name: Maralinga
runners_data.note: Five consecutive zero finishes on Good ground, all around the 10-19 range in the finishing order; a true hold-up runner fading into midfield placement with nothing in the form to suggest a reversal.

runners_data.name: Avandra
runners_data.note: Has a second on Good ground (2/16f) and three other placings, making him one of the more interesting low-OR hold-up types; however, he is naturally a hold-up runner in a field too full of them, limiting his ability to find a clean run.

runners_data.name: Doyen Og
runners_data.note: Listed as a hold-up runner with a fade flag and a run only seven days ago; Good-ground record shows one placing from 14 attempts and the blinkers haven't solved the problems — quick reappearance rings alarm bells.

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is a notable flag; ran a pulled-up run last time and three of five Good-ground runs returned unplaced — a hold-up type without a clear pathway through traffic.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who fades; won once at 18f on Good ground but has a zero last time and four 0/P/7 results recently — the drop to 2m1f is slightly short of what she has won over before.

runners_data.name: Stily
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with five placings in the last five runs including two seconds and two thirds; Good-ground form is the best in the field for a prominent type and this profile fits the dominant race shape very well.

races.paceDynamic: Gino Bella is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 26-runner field, likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset and control a sustainable, uncontested gallop around Cork's turning 2m1f. Getaway Henry and Cloudio are the most likely prominent companions, tracking Gino Bella in the early stages, while Stily is another who will press forward from a midfield vantage. With the pace moderate and uncontested, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel comfortably off the tempo and produce a late run — but critically, the field contains a large cluster of genuine hold-up types who cannot all get to the rear as they would wish. Footstepstoglory, Maxicourt, Let It Settle, Theanniversary Man and several others are true hold-up horses redistributed to a midfield slot on the map because the rear of the field will be impossibly congested; of these, Footstepstoglory and Theanniversary Man have the profile most likely to secure a workable position. The race shape ultimately favours horses with prominent or close-tracking ability — those who can sit just off Gino Bella's fractions, avoid trouble in the pack, and pick up over the final two flights without needing a long run from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gino Bella Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gino Bella sets a controlled, uncontested lead and the prominent trackers can settle just behind, the race is run at a rhythm that suits those who travel close to the pace.
scenarios.body: Gino Bella's fractions will be honest but not punishing on Good ground, and horses like Getaway Henry and Cloudio who travel with the pace will be first to pounce at the second-last; with so many genuine closers trapped in traffic behind, the front-to-prominent profile is the value position in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Gino Bella sets a slightly stronger early tempo and begins to weaken from two out, a close-tracking prominent runner who has conserved energy delivers the winning thrust.
scenarios.body: Stily's recent form shows consistent placing from a prominent position on Good ground and this trip, and Cloudio's profile suits tracking leaders; both are ideally placed to sweep past a fading leader without needing to weave through a congested pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses quickly after the last flight and the prominent horses hit a flat spot, a hold-up runner who has secured a workable position just off the rear can steal through.
scenarios.body: Eaglewood is lightly raced and handles Good ground well, while Theanniversary Man has shown winning form and, if he can navigate from midfield, his finishing effort is proven over similar trips; however, the crowded rear makes clean passage genuinely difficult in a 26-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If a cluster of prominent and midfield types collide for position mid-race causing traffic and interference, the race degenerates into a slow-motion finish where proven stayers grind out the result.
scenarios.body: With 26 runners over a turning track at Cork, pile-ups and crowding are plausible at the top of the straight; Theanniversary Man's two recent wins suggest he has the grit to find a way through trouble, and Eaglewood's Good-ground form over this exact distance could prove decisive in a messy scramble.

watchPoints.text: Gino Bella's lead is uncontested but the STYLE_FIT tag confirms he is out of natural role — watch whether the pace he sets is sustainable or whether he stops quickly from two out, opening the door for Getaway Henry or Stily.

With 26 runners on a turning Cork track, the congestion entering the straight is a major hazard — Theanniversary Man, Footstepstoglory and Lunar Landscape all need clear runs and could be fatally baulked.

Getaway Henry arrives in blinkers having won last time at 16f on Good ground — if he presses Gino Bella into a stronger gallop than expected, the race pace quickens and hold-up horses gain a better chance of catching the leaders flat-footed.

Jack Kennedy's ride on Laurie Blue deserves a second look — a top-level conditional booking on an 8-year-old hold-up type suggests connections believe conditions suit, and he could work his way into contention if traffic opens up.

Eaglewood is the most lightly exposed hold-up runner in the field with only nine similar-going runs and a win among them; a 277-day absence is the single question mark — if he has schooled well, he merits monitoring in-running.

races.name: Sign Up To Our Newsletter Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Brosna Queen
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who should bowl along uncontested; OR 113, recent course-and-distance win (Good), but her Prominent tag suggests she may actually race closer to the pace than truly leading — watch whether she is pushed to truly front-run or sits just off a notional leader.

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: 445 days absent (168-day forfeit flag) is a serious concern; flat form on Flat-type tracks at shorter distances offers little hurdles transferability, and her hold-up style leaves her reliant on a late surge this field is unlikely to set up.

runners_data.name: Arctic Flame
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on Good and placed again at the trip; Simon Torrens fits the horse, Patrick Foley's yard is 0/7 in the last 14 days but the mare's own form is solid — a genuine prominent contender who should secure a position just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Surfin Usa
runners_data.note: Won over 2m6f on Good last time and also placed over 2m2f on Good; Mullins/Hayes combination is 3/33 in the past fortnight, competitive strike rate — a proper prominent type who should slot behind Brosna Queen and is well suited by this controlled pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Early Bird
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on Good, placed at 2m3f on Soft; Sweeney yard 0/3 in 14 days; tongue-tie fitted; a prominent racer who has form at the trip and ground — needs to avoid the mid-race scrimmage to get the run his style ideally requires.

runners_data.name: Somersby Roost
runners_data.note: Won over 2m3f on Good last time out; prominent style suits this setup; tongue-tie fitted; 41 days since last run is fresh but not a concern — one of the more credible prominent contenders based purely on recent form and trip-and-ground combination.

runners_data.name: Diamond Tipp
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy booked is an obvious positive; recent form 338P-8 is modest; best form on Good at 2m2f and 2m6f but the 8-rated string on Good is a worry — a prominent racer who needs others to underperform.

runners_data.name: Costanuci
runners_data.note: Won't be the only one wanting prominent ground; true front-running type who has been pushed into midfield on the map because the prominent spots are oversubscribed — 0 wins from 15 similar-going runs is a brutal stat, and racing further back than he'd like makes improvement hard to find.

runners_data.name: Glitz And Glamour
runners_data.note: Won over 2m2f on Good; prominent style suits; Peter Smithers at 7lb claim is an unknown quantity in a competitive handicap — placed at 2m4f on Good so the trip is not a question, and represents a potential big-priced each-way runner if she avoids traffic.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Fades in finish flag is a red flag in a race where the pace is sustainable rather than searching; Harry Sexton 7lb claim; 0 wins and 0 placings from similar-going runs in the data — hold-up style into a modest pace is an unflattering combination.

runners_data.name: Lakewood Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (four fourths and a third from last five) but 0 wins; a genuine prominent type who is unlikely to secure her natural position in this crowded field, forced further back than ideal — the redistribution tag reflects a structural disadvantage, not a comment on ability.

runners_data.name: Evelyn
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has placed on Good going at 2m3f; tongue-tie and breast-plate fitted; 43 days since last run; her best chance would come if the pace collapses late, which a single-pacemaker scenario does not guarantee — situationally dependent.

runners_data.name: Felicity Smoak
runners_data.note: Returning from 195 days (33-day forfeit); Paul Nolan 3/16 in the fortnight is a reasonable yard stat but Felicity's own form on Good is poor (7/15); a hold-up type stepping from 2m to 2m4f with a question mark on stamina.

runners_data.name: Ellens Pride
runners_data.note: Fades in finish; won over 2m1f on Good but has not placed in five recent Good-ground runs; hold-up style is the wrong profile for a moderate-paced race — needs a searching gallop that Brosna Queen is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Loughrask Jet
runners_data.note: Fades in finish flag plus a redistribution from hold-up to midfield; 0 wins and 0 places from six Good-ground runs; a 5-year-old at OR 88 who has struggled to ever threaten — the combination of wrong style and weak form makes this a very tough ask.

runners_data.name: Tudorista
runners_data.note: 253 days off the track is a significant fitness question; a 4-year-old (light weight 144lbs) whose five Good-ground runs have produced a best of fourth; true hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map — Gavin Cromwell 4/34 in the fortnight but the horse needs to prove fitness first.

runners_data.name: Ballinearla Girl
runners_data.note: 83 days since last run; tongue-tie and breast-plate fitted; a natural prominent racer who cannot get her preferred berth in a field stacked with prominent types — Eoin Doyle 0/2 in 14 days; best effort (third on Soft) is below the level likely required here.

runners_data.name: Liss Eile
runners_data.note: True hold-up mare mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear of the field; best run is a fourth on Good at 2m; G Ahern 0/0 in 14 days; breast-plate fitted; a 2m specialist stepping up in trip and racing out of natural position — difficult to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Brosna Queen is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, she should bowl along at a sustainable gallop rather than a searching pace — this is a controlled, single-pacemaker scenario on Good ground over 2m4f. Behind her, Arctic Flame, Surfin Usa, Early Bird, Somersby Roost, Diamond Tipp and Glitz And Glamour are all natural prominent racers competing for the same handful of positions just off the lead, creating a compressed, traffic-heavy mid-section. Costanuci, Lakewood Rose and Ballinearla Girl are genuine prominent types who are unlikely to secure their natural berth and have been mapped to midfield by necessity — the front five or six slots will be claimed by higher-rated, better-drawn rivals before they can assert. The race shape therefore favours patient, prominent-to-midfield horses who can sit just behind the scrimmage and produce a clean run in the straight, rather than true hold-up closers who will face an even harder task threading through 18 runners off a moderate pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Brosna Queen sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent pack settles without incident, the race sets up for a horse travelling prominently just off the leader.
scenarios.body: Surfin Usa or Arctic Flame, both natural prominent racers with Good-ground form and quality handlers, can stalk the pace, avoid the mid-race traffic and produce their finish in the straight; a moderate pace suits horses who get into it early rather than those making up ground from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Falters, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Brosna Queen's solo lead produces a false pace that suddenly quickens late, creating a wall of tiring horses in the straight for closers to dodge.
scenarios.body: A midfield runner who travels sweetly and finds a clear path in the straight — such as Glitz And Glamour or Evelyn — could benefit if the prominent pack has emptied earlier than expected; this is more plausible than a pure hold-up scenario because the closers are not far back in a single-pacemaker race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Chaos Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack jostles for position early and the pace is more contested than it appears, creating carnage in the field and a messy race.
scenarios.body: Any runner who finds a clean passage — likely Somersby Roost or Early Bird, both placed on Good ground at this trip — could sprint clear while rivals are caught in traffic; this scenario rewards horses who have been ridden quietly without needing to fight for position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack burns each other out and a lower-rated, patient runner exploits the moderate pace with a clear run late.
scenarios.body: Liss Eile or Ballinearla Girl, both redistributed from their natural prominent role, are unlikely to win from a disadvantaged position, but a completely clear run could see a calmer-travelling outsider sneak into the frame; this scenario is the least likely given the going, the pace setup and the quality of the higher-rated prominent types.

watchPoints.text: Surfin Usa (Mullins/Hayes) arrives on the back of a Good-ground win and gets a prominent position by right — watch whether Brian Hayes slots straight into second or third behind Brosna Queen at the first hurdle, as that would confirm the race shape is playing into his hands.

The scrum for prominent positions between Arctic Flame, Early Bird, Somersby Roost and Diamond Tipp immediately after the start is the key chaos point — any of these four bumping or being checked in the first half-mile could dramatically alter the result.

Costanuci, Lakewood Rose and Ballinearla Girl are all genuine prominent types who have been mapped to midfield; if any of them pushes forward aggressively early they could increase the pace beyond what Brosna Queen and the prominent pack can handle, turning a controlled race into a more demanding one.

Preparations (445 days absent, Flat pedigree, hold-up style) and Tudorista (253 days absent) are both returning from very long layoffs — monitor market moves close to post time as any support for either would suggest stable confidence that the form data cannot reflect.

Felicity Smoak is the youngest runner (4yo) in the field and steps up from 2m to 2m4f on her return from 195 days; Paul Nolan's recent yard form is reasonable but the stamina question over this extra distance on Good ground is worth tracking if she is prominent early.

races.name: Follow Us On X Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ajp Falco
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish; five-year-old returning at 33 days, has form over today's good ground but a worrying recent string of pulled-up and failed runs, and the 24f trip today is the longest he has faced — stamina a real concern.

runners_data.name: C Pas Possible
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run recorded, a placed effort at 24f on good ground — actually encouraging course-distance profile; Phillip Enright a competent booking, and the sparse form makes assessment difficult but this trip could suit a fresh recruit.

runners_data.name: Jeroboam Machin
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has already won twice at lesser distances on soft and heavy; stepping up markedly in trip and surface condition today, but Emmet Mullins has placed him shrewdly before and a handy, jumping-efficient style suits the likely steady-pace scenario well.

runners_data.name: Mind Eraser
runners_data.note: Style unknown given very limited public form; amateur jockey booking and a trainer with no recent winners in the 14-day window; last run recorded as a point-to-point pull-up, making pace map placement guesswork — treat as a rank unknown.

runners_data.name: Riverstown Boy
runners_data.note: Unplaced in all five starts with a pattern of mid-field finishes on good ground; returned only eight days ago, which is an aggressive turnaround, and consistent failure to improve or get competitive makes it hard to construct a winning case in any scenario.

runners_data.name: The Boysofairhill
runners_data.note: Hold-up seven-year-old whose most recent form reads 5-8-0-7 on good ground — he simply hasn't threatened in a while; Shane Fitzgerald rides, but finishing positions have trended the wrong way and this is a horse that needs things to fall perfectly from the back of the field.

runners_data.name: Withabitofluk
runners_data.note: Prominent type from the Henry de Bromhead yard, which has a strong 14-day strike rate (11/35); his best run was a second at 20f on good ground, and a step up to 3m today with a young claiming jockey could test him, but the trainer's form and the pace scenario suit his hold-close style.

runners_data.name: Young Doran
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the race, he shaped well for a second on his only start at 22f on good ground; Shane O'Callaghan takes the ride, and while the STYLE_FIT flag suggests he may be racing slightly out of role positionally, in practice he is the one horse certain to lead — sustainable fractions are to his advantage.

runners_data.name: Deerpark Lassie
runners_data.note: Very limited public information — no last-run date recorded, no form string supplied, and a reduced weight of 159lbs; from the David Harry Kelly yard (who also saddle Ajp Falco), this runner must be treated as a complete unknown until market moves reveal anything.

runners_data.name: Howyasox
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old with a consistent pattern of mid-to-rear finishes in the six-to-eight range on good ground; the amateur 7lb claimer booking does not inspire, and nothing in his record suggests he can raise his level significantly stepping up to 3m.

runners_data.name: Pegasuslane
runners_data.note: A hold-up type wearing a hood, flagged as a horse who fades in the closing stages — a worrying combination for a 3m maiden; only two recorded runs, one of which was a pull-up, and the going has always been good, so stamina doubts are real.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner is the classiest trainer entry in the race with Jack Kennedy in the saddle — a potent combination; form of 3-P-2-6-3 shows he stays and places, and two placed efforts on good ground at trips up to 22f suggest today's 3m is workable. Kennedy's ability to judge pace makes him a live threat in a steadily-run contest.

runners_data.name: Star Cave
runners_data.note: Unknown style with very limited public form and a 229-day absence — a significant layoff that introduces considerable uncertainty; the tongue-tie is noted, Patrick Foley has one winner in 14 days from seven runners, and the long break alone is enough to flag this as a horse needing to be taken on trust.

races.paceDynamic: Young Doran is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 13-runner maiden hurdle over 3 miles at Cork, and with no other horse likely to push for the lead, he should be able to bowl along at a controlled, unhurried tempo on good ground. Jeroboam Machin and Sound Judgement are the other prominent types who will look to track the gallop from close range, but neither has the profile or the mandate to force a contentious early pace. With just one genuine front-runner setting a sustainable clip over three miles on a flat, fair track, the race is unlikely to be run at a searching enough gallop to fully test the hold-up horses, and those who travel prominently or just off the pace will be able to conserve energy and pounce. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and patient mid-division types who travel fluently, as the steady tempo will compress the field and reward those with a clear passage turning for home rather than those who need a true test of stamina to get competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Young Doran controls proceedings at a comfortable clip and nothing raises the tempo materially before the home turn.
scenarios.body: Young Doran sets a sustainable fractions over 3m, leaving those tracking him in touch with minimal expenditure; a prominent or handy horse who travels well and jumps cleanly will be perfectly placed to pick off the leader in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just deceptive enough over 3m to stretch the field and deliver late finishers from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop over this trip — even at steady tempo — can tax the leader and those prominent early if they race keenly, opening a lane for hold-up types who find the extra distance in their favour.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks
scenarios.trigger: If Young Doran is left entirely alone to dictate a frugal tempo and simply idles home from the front.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied and a generous pace, Young Doran could exploit an uncontested lead on good ground over 3m and prove difficult to reel in for those who leave it too late; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers this, but the raw scenario remains viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the race is disrupted by jumping errors, fallers, or a dramatically uneven pace that fragments the field.
scenarios.body: A frantic or stop-start gallop over 3m breaks the race open for whoever avoids trouble and jumps cleanly down the back; lightly-raced unknowns with fresh legs could capitalise on a muddled contest.

watchPoints.text: Young Doran's tempo will define this race — if Shane O'Callaghan elects to exploit the lone lead and quickens early on the home turn, hold-up types like Ajp Falco and Howyasox may find the race over before they get competitive.

Sound Judgement (Jack Kennedy/Gordon Elliott) is the most dangerous combination in the race on paper — watch the market for any significant move that would signal confidence from the stable in this straightforward pace scenario.

Jeroboam Machin's jumping accuracy will be key over 3m at Cork; if he gets into a fluent rhythm from a prominent position, his twice-winning profile over shorter gives him the engine to quicken — a bad jump anywhere in the back straight could end his chance instantly.

Deerpark Lassie has no recorded form or last-run date — monitor the market closely before race time as any unusual move for this complete unknown from the Kelly yard should not be ignored in a weak maiden field.

Several runners — including Riverstown Boy (8 days) and The Boysofairhill (7 days) — have had very recent outings; fatigue or residual soreness from quick turnarounds over a 3m trip on good ground could cause unexpected early losses of position or jumping errors in the middle of the race.

races.name: RBC Brewin Dolphin Hurdle

runners_data.name: Happy Jacky
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer aged 12 with solid Good-ground form and a course win at 24f; Peter Smithers' 7lb claim is a notable booking, 46 days off is fine, and the OR of 140 keeps him competitive — sits close to Maxxum as the key pace-chasing danger.

runners_data.name: Hewick
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has been in poor form (457P9), now 71 days off for John Joseph Hanlon, and a Going record of only 10/15 in similar conditions; the high rating of 145 flatters current form and the lack of recent wins on Good ground is a flag.

runners_data.name: Reverend Hubert
runners_data.note: 315 days off the track is a serious concern, but C Byrnes has him fit enough to run and he has winning form at 16f and 18f on Good — a true hold-up horse who is unproven at this 3m trip but capable of finishing strongly if the layoff hasn't blunted him.

runners_data.name: Smooth Tom
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who won over 18f on Good ground and has solid placed form; Andrew Slattery's yard is in form (3/39 over 14 days) and Cian Quirke is a capable handler — needs a race that develops late for his stamina to tell.

runners_data.name: Topgun Simmy
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a big engine — won twice over 22f and 26f on Good, 326 days off the track is the significant query, but John Joseph Hanlon sends him out in form (T14: 2/19) and Donagh Meyler is a solid appointment at prominent weight.

runners_data.name: Da Capo Glory
runners_data.note: Consistent placer over 23-25f on Good, two runner-up finishes recently, wearing a hood (headgear noted) — Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps the weight, but zero wins from similar conditions makes a break-through slightly against the grain here.

runners_data.name: Desert Cave
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, pushed into midfield on the pace map because of field compression — OR of 102 is the lowest in the race and recent form reads 565-00, making it hard to see a winning run materialising regardless of where it ends up tactically.

runners_data.name: Linden Arden
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer by inclination but displaced into midfield given how many runners want that position; Brian Hayes takes the ride for David Harry Kelly, 110 days off, and only 2 wins from 7 GOO-ground runs — real-style disadvantage in this shape counts against him.

runners_data.name: Maxxum
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 146, ridden by Jack Kennedy for Gordon Elliott who is firing (8/48 over 14 days) — the confirmed pace-setter over 3m on Good ground, but his sim-going record is a concern (6/15, 0 wins on Good), and the STYLE_FIT flag suggests he may not be entirely comfortable leading at this distance.

runners_data.name: Roi Mage
runners_data.note: Aged 14 and a natural prominent racer, but the field shape pushes him off that position; only 1/15 similar-going runs and no wins on Good ground in recent history — Harry Sexton's 7lb claim is a positive weight factor but the age and going record work against him.

runners_data.name: Mousey Brown
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by trade, wearing a tongue-tie, and carrying only 147lbs with Alix Balfe's 7lb claim — compressed into midfield rather than his preferred rear position; recent form (455F-4) is modest but he stays well over 24f on Good and could be involved late if the race truly falls apart in front of him.

races.paceDynamic: Maxxum is the confirmed and likely uncontested pace-setter here, with Jack Kennedy expected to dictate from the front over this 3m trip on Good ground at Cork — a sustainable gallop rather than a lung-bursting pace is the likely outcome. With Topgun Gunny, Happy Jacky, and Da Capo Glory all genuine prominent types, there will be pressure for the first few positions just off Maxxum, though none are likely to seriously challenge him for the lead itself. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their natural positions — Linden Arden and Roi Mage are genuine prominent racers who will be pushed further back than they'd like, while Mousey Brown and Desert Cave are true hold-up types similarly compressed into midfield rather than tracking from the rear. This race shape — one controlled front-runner setting a measured pace — strongly favours hold-up horses with the class and stamina to close ground late, or any prominent runner close enough to pounce without being drawn into a draining battle for early position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Maxxum Dictates, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Maxxum leads comfortably at a fair pace and the field cannot reel him in late.
scenarios.body: Jack Kennedy sets a measured tempo from the front, and on Good ground over 3m the race turns into a test of stamina and jumping accuracy rather than a sprint finish; prominent horses close enough to Maxxum throughout are best placed to challenge. Topgun Simmy and Happy Jacky, sitting just off the pace, are the profile types most likely to benefit from this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sustainable and a quality hold-up runner picks off the leaders from the rear in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Smooth Tom or Hewick, both genuine hold-up horses with proven stamina at this sort of trip, would need to be produced with a strong late run after Maxxum and the prominent horses have done the hard work. Good ground suits both, and the 3m trip gives them enough distance to close — though they must genuinely be able to get to the front rather than from a compressed midfield position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply in the back straight and the front-runners burn each other out, allowing a close-tracking challenger to dominate.
scenarios.body: An uptick in pace from any of the prominent runners nearest Maxxum would compress the race and reward a horse sitting handy with a good cruising speed; Da Capo Glory's recent placed form over similar trips makes her the profile type here, while Happy Jacky's experience over the course and distance is relevant. This shape is somewhat less likely given the pace analysis suggests Maxxum is unlikely to be seriously pressured.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Unsettles Favourites
scenarios.trigger: If there are jumping errors or positional scrimmaging in the early stages that disrupt the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With several horses compressed out of their natural positions, interference or a loose runner could create gaps that allow an unconsidered runner such as Reverend Hubert — who has course-distance winning form — to emerge from the pack. This scenario is low probability given the controlled nature expected, but the presence of headgear-wearing horses and two 7lb claimer combinations adds a marginal unpredictability factor.

watchPoints.text: Maxxum (Jack Kennedy) going completely unchallenged up front — if Elliott's stable star is allowed to bowl along at his own pace on Good ground, the gap to the prominent pack could prove insurmountable by the final hurdle.

Linden Arden and Roi Mage — both genuine prominent types forced back into midfield; watch for early scrimmaging as they attempt to push forward from their drawn positions, which could disrupt the rhythm of horses around them.

Reverend Hubert returning from 315 days off — C Byrnes runners on long lay-offs can be fresh and ready, but a jumping error after such a break at a testing 3m trip is a credible risk that would compromise any late challenge.

Hewick at OR 145 is the highest-rated hold-up horse in the field but arrives in poor recent form across six runs — watch whether Paddy Hanlon (5) settles him early, as a flat-spot or jumping error could confirm he is not at his peak.

Desert Cave and Mousey Brown — two horses racing effectively out of their natural hold-up roles and placed in midfield on the map — monitor whether they drift further back at the start, which would confirm the pace shape is even more straightforward for Maxxum than it appears.
